topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the scope of the lecture on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate recognition through molecular patterns and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system senses infection and tissue damage using molecular patterns and their corresponding receptor and signaling pathways.

topics.label: Acute inflammatory response, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic complications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate acute inflammation, coordinate leukocyte recruitment into tissues, and drive systemic consequences such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are stopped, how tissues are repaired, and how persistent inflammatory stimuli lead to chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the next lecture.
